items.title: 3.6.1 Molecular orbital diagrams of some diatomic molecules and their bond orders

source_refs.note: Topic 3.6.1, printed pages 65-67 (Figures 3.36 to 3.38). The print's 'figure 36' for oxygen is Figure 3.38; its oxygen bond order is printed as '2( )' with the fraction lost.

blocks.text: The configuration of He is 1s2. For He2 to form, the 1s orbitals of two helium atoms must combine into a bonding sigma 1s and an antibonding sigma* 1s orbital. Of the four electrons, two enter the bonding orbital and the remaining two the antibonding orbital, so the bond order of He2 is (2 - 2) / 2 = 0; hence the He2 molecule is not formed.

blocks.alt: Energy arrow on the left. 2He = 1s with a pair of electrons on each side, each tagged A.O. In the middle, sigma* (1s) above, tagged A.B.M.O, and sigma (1s) below, tagged B.M.O, each holding a pair of opposite arrows.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.36: Molecular orbital diagram of He2 molecule (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.36).

blocks.text: Nitrogen is 1s2 2s2 2px1 2py1 2pz1. The valence 2s orbitals of the two atoms give sigma 2s and sigma* 2s, while the 2p orbitals give six molecular orbitals in increasing order of energy: sigma 2s < sigma* 2s < pi 2py = pi 2pz < sigma 2px < pi* 2py = pi* 2pz < sigma* 2px. The bond order of N2 from its diagram is (6 - 0) / 2 = 3, so there are three covalent bonds between the nitrogen atoms, one sigma and two pi: a triple bond.

blocks.alt: Energy arrow on the left. Upper part: 7N = 2pz 2py 2px on each side, one up arrow in each, tagged A.O. Molecular orbitals from bottom: pi(2py) and pi(2pz) each with a pair, sigma(2px) with a pair (B.M.O); pi*(2py), pi*(2pz) and sigma*(2px) empty (A.B.M.O). Lower part: 7N = 2s with a pair on each side (A.O), sigma(2s) with a pair (B.M.O) and sigma*(2s) with a pair (A.B.M.O).
blocks.caption: Figure 3.37: Molecular orbital diagram of N2 molecule (original drawing after the textbook's Fig 3.37).

blocks.text: For oxygen the energies of the molecular orbitals are arranged sigma 2s < sigma* 2s < sigma 2px < pi 2py = pi 2pz < pi* 2py = pi* 2pz < sigma* 2px. The bond order of oxygen is 2, which shows one sigma and one pi bond between the oxygen atoms, a double bond O=O. The oxygen molecule is paramagnetic: it is attracted by a magnetic field, and liquid oxygen is attracted and suspended between the poles of a strong magnet. Paramagnetic substances have one or more unpaired electrons, and a substance with many unpaired electrons is strongly paramagnetic. MOT explains this behaviour: the MO diagram of oxygen shows two unpaired electrons, one each in pi* 2py and pi* 2pz, which give the molecule a net magnetic field that interacts with an external field.

blocks.alt: Energy arrow on the left. Upper part: 8O = 2pz 2py 2px on the left with one up arrow, one up arrow and a pair, and the mirror order on the right, tagged A.O. Molecular orbitals from bottom: sigma(2px) with a pair, pi(2py) and pi(2pz) each with a pair (B.M.O); pi*(2py) and pi*(2pz) with one up arrow each and sigma*(2px) empty (A.B.M.O). Lower part: 8O = 2s pairs (A.O), sigma(2s) and sigma*(2s) each with a pair.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.38: Molecular orbital diagram of O2 molecule (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.38).
